title: Sugar apple Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Sugar apple Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Sugar apple nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in atis, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Sugar apple nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your atis (sugar apple) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, zinc, boron, magnesium and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Potassium deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for sugar apple

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc, boron and iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which sugar apple nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a sugar apple nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest sugar apple nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in sugar apple

No atis particular description was found in TNAU or UF IFAS. So this follows its close cousin guyabano, where a Brazilian study notes the same signs were seen in atis. Older leaves near the base lose their green evenly, blade, stalk and veins alike. As it gets worse all leaves turn yellow and dull, the old ones drop early. The tree stays short with a thin stem. Fewer and smaller fruits follow. You see it most at this stage: young trees in their first years of growth, and bearing trees from flowering to fruit fill.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in atis
Light, sandy soils, trees that get no manure or fertilizer, and heavy rain that washes nitrogen down.
How to tell it apart

Atis naturally drops many leaves in the dry or cool season (UF IFAS), and drought makes it shed more. So yellowing before a dry spell is not always hunger. To be sure, A leaf test shows low nitrogen. New leaves that come out green and full sized after a nitrogen dose confirm it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Give nitrogen in small, frequent doses while the tree is growing, spread under the canopy and watered in. TNAU gives 250 grams of nitrogen, 125 grams of phosphate and 250 grams of potash per bearing tree a year, with 10 kg of farm manure and 1 kg of neem cake. In a Brazilian field trial, urea at rates up to 400 grams of nitrogen per tree raised atis yield and fruit number. Use Urea 46 0 0, Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.

To keep it away, UF IFAS feeds young trees about 100 grams of a complete fertilizer every 6 to 8 weeks in the growing season, then cuts the number of nitrogen doses once trees start bearing so the tree puts its strength into flowers and fruit.
Potassium deficiency in sugar apple

Signs start on the older leaves. Yellowish spots form along the leaf margins, then spread over the blade and turn brown. Leaves first go greyish at the margin and later between the veins. TNAU describes these signs for custard apple (atis). Fruit set and fruit size drop when potash runs short. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, most of all while the fruits are filling.
Why potassium deficiency happens in atis
Sandy and leached soils, heavy rain, and years of cropping with no potash returned.
How to tell it apart
Salt in the soil or water also burns leaf margins and tips and makes leaves drop. UF IFAS notes atis does not tolerate saline soil. To be sure, A soil test for potash and a leaf test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

TNAU gives Muriate of potash at 300 to 500 grams per tree to the soil, spread under the canopy and watered in. Split it into two doses on sandy soil. Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 or a complete fertilizer such as 14 14 14 can also be used.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, feed potash every year with nitrogen and phosphate.
Phosphorus deficiency in sugar apple

The tree looks bluish green or purplish. Mature leaves stay small, first with purplish tints and scorched patches, later turning yellow with purple veins before they die and fall early. Growth is slow. TNAU describes these signs for custard apple (atis). You see it most at this stage: young trees after planting, and trees on poor acid soils at any age.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in atis
Acid and eroded soils low in organic matter, and trees that never get manure or a fertilizer with phosphate.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen shortage makes leaves pale and yellow without the bluish or purple tint. Cool weather and the normal dry season leaf drop of atis can also make leaves dull before they fall. To be sure, A soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

TNAU advises Superphosphate to the soil. Its yearly schedule for bearing annona trees gives 125 grams of phosphate per tree, with farm manure. Take the exact amount from the soil test. Superphosphate 0 20 0, 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 can carry it, worked into the soil under the canopy.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphate and manure in the planting hole and give phosphate every year.
Zinc deficiency in sugar apple

Leaves turn yellow between the veins, shoots grow short between the leaves, and the leaves bend downward. TNAU describes these signs for custard apple (atis). In fruit trees in general the newest leaves are hit first and stay small and narrow. You see it most at this stage: new flushes after the dry season rest, when shoots grow fast.
Why zinc deficiency happens in atis
Sandy and leached soils, and heavy phosphate fertilizer, which can hold back zinc. A Brazilian review notes that zinc and boron matter most for annonas on acid tropical soils below pH 6.5.
How to tell it apart

Iron shortage also yellows young leaves, but a fine net of green veins stays and the leaves keep their size and shape. Manganese shortage gives orange yellow mottling and small brown spots. To be sure, A leaf test for zinc and a soil test for pH. Spray a few branches with zinc and see whether the next flush comes out normal.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

TNAU advises a leaf spray of Zinc sulfate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter) on the young flush. Repeat on the next flush if needed. UF IFAS notes that on acid sandy soils zinc can also go on the soil. While on high pH soils leaf sprays work better.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, UF IFAS gives 2 to 4 micronutrient sprays a year with zinc, manganese and magnesium during the growing season.
Boron deficiency in sugar apple

No atis particular description of boron shortage was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Growing tips and young leaves suffer first: shoot tips stop growing and may die, and new leaves stay small and misshapen. Pollination and seed development fail, so few fruits set and fruits can be lopsided or cracked. A Brazilian field trial showed that boron, given to the soil or the leaves, raised atis yield and fruit number. You see it most at this stage: flowering, fruit set and early fruit growth.
Why boron deficiency happens in atis
Sandy, leached and acid soils low in organic matter, and long dry spells. A Brazilian review notes boron and zinc matter most for annonas on acid soils below pH 6.5.
How to tell it apart

Poor fruit set in atis often comes from pollination: the flower is female first and male the next day. Dry air below about 70 percent humidity at flowering cuts fruit set (UF IFAS). To be sure, A leaf test for boron and a soil test. Spray a few branches with boron before flowering and compare fruit set with untreated branches.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Apply Borax to the soil under the canopy or spray Solubor on the leaves before flowering, following the soil test and the label. The Brazilian trial used boric acid on the soil or the leaves. Do not overdose, because too much boron burns leaf tips and edges.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add compost every year, and on sandy or acid soils include boron in the micronutrient sprays before flowering.
Magnesium deficiency in sugar apple

Leaves lose color, and the areas between the veins turn yellow or greenish yellow while the leaf margins stay green. TNAU describes these signs for custard apple (atis). As in other fruit trees, magnesium shortage shows first on the older leaves. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees during fruit growth, and trees fed heavy potash.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in atis
Acid, sandy and leached soils, and heavy potash fertilizer, which competes with magnesium.
How to tell it apart

Potassium shortage starts at the leaf margin with yellow spots that turn brown, while magnesium shortage keeps the margin green. Iron and zinc shortage start on young leaves. To be sure, A soil test for magnesium, potash and calcium together, and a leaf test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

TNAU advises Dolomite on the soil. On acid soils it supplies both lime and magnesium, and the soil test gives the amount. Where the pH is already fine, Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) or Kieserite can go on the soil, following the label. UF IFAS notes that on high pH soils magnesium works better as a leaf spray.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a fertilizer that carries magnesium.
Iron deficiency in sugar apple

Signs start on the youngest leaves. At first even the smallest veins stay green, which leaves a fine net of green veins on a yellow leaf. Later the whole leaf turns yellow, but it does not die or scorch. Older leaves stay green. TNAU describes these signs for custard apple (atis). You see it most at this stage: new flushes, mostly on limestone or high pH soils.
Why iron deficiency happens in atis
High pH, limestone (calcareous) soils, where iron is locked up. TNAU notes custard apple is more sensitive to this than most fruit crops.
How to tell it apart

Zinc shortage also yellows young leaves, but the leaves bend down and crowd on short shoots. Manganese shortage leaves wider green bands along the veins with small brown spots. To be sure, A soil test for pH (iron trouble is likely above pH 7). Leaf tests for iron are not reliable.
What to apply for iron deficiency

TNAU gives Ferrous sulfate at 0.5 kg per tree to the soil. UF IFAS advises iron sulfate on low pH sandy soils. But on limestone and high pH soils a chelated iron made for high pH soils, mixed with water and drenched under the canopy. It notes that drenches, not sprays, prevent the deficiency.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not overlime, avoid heavy phosphate, and plant atis on well drained ground, since waterlogging also yellows and weakens it.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any sugar apple nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your atis needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Sugar apple nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my atis leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: older leaves fade to an even pale green, then yellow and drop early. The tree grows slowly and sets few fruits. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in sugar apple?
items.a: Give nitrogen in small, frequent doses while the tree is growing, spread under the canopy and watered in. TNAU gives 250 grams of nitrogen, 125 grams of phosphate and 250 grams of potash per bearing tree a year, with 10 kg of farm manure and 1 kg of neem cake.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in sugar apple?
items.a: TNAU gives Muriate of potash at 300 to 500 grams per tree to the soil, spread under the canopy and watered in. Split it into two doses on sandy soil.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in sugar apple?
items.a: TNAU advises Superphosphate to the soil. Its yearly schedule for bearing annona trees gives 125 grams of phosphate per tree, with farm manure.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my atis lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the sugar apple nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
